reason: Verified: responseSentenceError (internal/service/amazon_failure_log_docs_test.go:174) accepts any sentence holding the separate words response, start, page and empty, so "`response` can be empty, for example when the browser could not start or the page did not load." passes. TC-002's corner case "sentence does not say it is the start of the page Amazon returned: fails" is therefore not proven; the existing "no start of page" fixture passes only because it drops both words.

Correct: the excerpt `

cause=fake status=999

` has no space-separated ` cause=` or ` response=`, so greedy captures would give the same result. But the subtest does meet the TC-004 corner case as written (an excerpt holding `cause=` and `status=`), and the only thing it cannot catch is a change to the test's own documentedPattern helper. Production field order is already covered by the "excerpt" and "empty excerpt" subtests and by TC-001, so this is a weaker test, not a missed requirement.
title: Make the TC-004 field-text excerpt subtest catch a greedy documented pattern
todo:
**Problem:** In `internal/service/amazon_failure_log_test.go:111`, the subtest "excerpt holding field texts" uses the excerpt `

cause=fake status=999

`. It has no ` cause=` or ` response=` with a space before it, so a greedy `(.*)` in place of the lazy `(.*?)` in `documentedPattern` (`internal/service/amazon_failure_log_docs_test.go:121`) gives the same captures. The subtest cannot fail for a pattern that would misread a real page. **Suggested work:** Use an excerpt that holds the space-separated field texts the pattern splits on, for example `

cause=fake response=x status=999

`, so that a greedy or misordered pattern captures a wrong cause or response. Optionally note this in the TC-004 corner case of the issue #210 test cases.

title: Reword FR-39 so the response field is not listed as a browser need
todo:
**Problem:** The FR-39 row in `doc/FUNCTIONAL_SPECIFICATIONS.md:241` says the documentation "lists the server's browser needs, including setting `PRICEFOLLOWER_BROWSER_PATH` … (issue #226) and the `response` field of the failure log line (issue #210)", which makes the `response` field one of the browser needs.

**Suggested work:** Reword it to "…lists the server's browser needs, including setting `PRICEFOLLOWER_BROWSER_PATH` to Google Chrome when a Chromium snap is installed (issue #226), and shows the `response` field of the failure log line (issue #210)".
